problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{x-y},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-1.$
worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=-1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{z}{x-y} & =-1 \\ z & =y-x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=-1$ is the plane $z=y-x.$
